# Additions to Esther Chapter 3 (Addition C) — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Additions to Esther C | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/ADE_003_page_001.jpg

---

*[Addition C: The prayers of Mordecai and Esther. Inserted after Hebrew Esther 4:17. This is the theological heart of Greek Esther — God is explicitly named and invoked for the first time.]*

**3:1** And Mordecai prayed to-the Lord, remembering all the-works of-the Lord, and said:

**3:2** "O Lord, Lord, almighty King, for all things are in your power, and there-is no-one who-can oppose you in your will to-save Israel.

**3:3** For you made the-heaven and the-earth and every marvelous thing under the-heaven.

**3:4** You are Lord of all, and there-is no-one who-can resist you — the Lord.

**3:5** You know all things. You know, Lord, that not in insolence nor in pride nor in vain-glory did I do this — to-refuse-to-bow-down to the arrogant Haman.

**3:6** For I would-have-been-willing to-kiss the soles of his feet for the-sake-of the-salvation of Israel.

**3:7** But I did this lest I should-set the glory of a man above the glory of God, and I-will-not bow down to any except to you, who-are my God and Lord; and I-will-not do these-things in pride.

**3:8** And now, O Lord God and King, God of Abraham, spare your people, for they-are looking upon us to-destroy us, and they-desire to-utterly-destroy the-inheritance that-was yours from-the beginning.

**3:9** Do-not overlook your portion, which you-redeemed for yourself out-of-the land of Egypt.

**3:10** Hear my prayer and have-mercy on your inheritance, and turn our mourning into feasting, that we-may-live and sing-praise to your name, O Lord; and do-not destroy the mouth of-the ones-praising you, O Lord."

**3:11** And all Israel cried out mightily, for their death was before them.

**3:12** And Queen Esther, being-seized-with-anguish, fled to-the Lord.

**3:13** And having-taken-off her glorious garments, she-put-on garments of distress and mourning, and instead of-the costly perfumes she-covered her head with ashes and dung, and she-humbled her body greatly, and all the-places of her gladsome adornment she-filled with the-tangles of her disheveled [hair].

**3:14** And she-prayed to-the Lord God of Israel and said:

**3:15** "O my Lord, you alone are our King. Help me, who-am-alone and who-have no helper except you,

**3:16** for my danger is in my hand.

**3:17** From my childhood I have-heard in the-tribe of my fathers that you, O Lord, took Israel out of all the-nations, and our fathers from all their ancestors, as an everlasting inheritance; and you-did for them all that you-promised.

**3:18** And now we-sinned before you, and you-gave us into the-hands of our enemies,

**3:19** because we-glorified their gods. You are righteous, O Lord.

**3:20** And now they-are-not satisfied with the-bitterness of our slavery, but have-put their hands on the-hands of their idols,

**3:21** to-abolish the-ordinance of your mouth and to-destroy your inheritance and to-stop the-mouth of those-praising you and to-extinguish the-glory of your house and your altar,

**3:22** and to-open the-mouths of-the nations for-the praise of vain idols and to-magnify a mortal king for ever.

**3:23** Do-not yield, O Lord, your scepter to those-who-are not, and let them not mock at our fall; but turn their counsel against themselves, and make an example of him who-began against us.

**3:24** Remember us, O Lord. Make yourself known in-the time of our tribulation, and give me courage, O King of-the gods and Master of all dominion.

**3:25** Put eloquent speech in my mouth before the-lion, and turn his heart to-hate the-one who-fights against us, so that there-be an-end to him and to those-who-agree with him.

**3:26** But save us by your hand, and help me, who-am alone and who-have no-helper except you, O Lord.

**3:27** You have knowledge of all things, and you know that I hate the glory of lawless ones and I-abhor the-bed of the-uncircumcised and of every foreigner.

**3:28** You know my necessity — that I abhor the sign of my arrogance, which is upon my head in-the days of my public-appearance; and I abhor it as a cloth of-menstruation, and I-do-not wear it in-the days of my quiet.

**3:29** And your servant has-not eaten at the-table of Haman, and I-did-not honor the-feast of-the king, and I-did-not drink the-wine of libations.

**3:30** And your servant has-had no joy from the-day of my change until-now, except in you, O Lord God of Abraham.

**3:31** O God, who-are mighty above all, hear the-voice of the-despairing, and save us from the-hand of the-evil-ones, and deliver me from my fear."
